# PropertySG — joetay.com

> Singapore residential property advisory run by Joe Tay, a CEA-registered salesperson
> with ERA Realty Network. The site publishes data-backed HDB resale prices for all 26
> HDB towns, verified new-launch project records, and buyer/seller guides. Price figures
> derive from the official data.gov.sg HDB resale dataset under the Singapore Open Data
> Licence; each project record carries the date it was last verified.

## Common questions

> Each answer is quoted word for word from the linked guide; see the guide for the official sources.

- Does selling an HDB flat take only eight weeks? No. HDB describes completion as about eight weeks after it accepts the resale application. Finding a buyer, the OTP stage and submitting a complete application happen before that clock starts. ([How Long to Sell an HDB Flat in Singapore?](https://joetay.com/insights/how-long-to-sell-hdb-singapore-2026.html))
- When do I receive the money from selling my HDB flat? At resale completion. HDB says cash proceeds are credited to your bank account by the next working day after completion, and it arranges the CPF refund within 7–14 working days of the appointment. If you appoint a private solicitor, the solicitor arranges the CPF refund. ([How to Sell an HDB Flat: Steps, Fees & Proceeds](https://joetay.com/insights/how-to-sell-hdb-flat-singapore.html))
- How much does an HDB valuation cost, and who pays? The buyer pays HDB a $120 processing fee, including GST, for a Request for Value; the seller does not pay it. The fee is non-refundable. The result applies to that OTP and is valid for three months from availability in the HDB Flat Portal; the resale application must be submitted within that period. ([HDB Valuation: $120 Fee, Process & Who Pays](https://joetay.com/insights/hdb-valuation-explained.html))
- When does the 5-year MOP start? For a new flat, MOP generally starts at key collection; for a resale flat, at resale completion. Periods of non-occupation can be excluded. The applicable period depends on the flat and purchase conditions, so confirm HDB's recorded eligibility date rather than adding five years yourself. ([Selling HDB After MOP: 5-Step Timeline (2026)](https://joetay.com/insights/selling-hdb-after-mop-singapore.html))
- How much is Seller’s Stamp Duty in Singapore? For a home bought on or after 4 July 2025, SSD is 16% if sold within one year, 12% in the second year, 8% in the third and 4% in the fourth. For a home bought between 11 March 2017 and 3 July 2025 it is 12%, 8% and 4% over three years. It is charged on the higher of the selling price and market value. ([Seller’s Stamp Duty Singapore: Rates & Rules](https://joetay.com/insights/seller-stamp-duty-singapore.html))
- Do I need to meet an MOP before selling a private condo? No. Private condos have no Minimum Occupation Period. Check Seller’s Stamp Duty instead: it applies if you sell within four years of a purchase made on or after 4 July 2025, or within three years of one made between 11 March 2017 and 3 July 2025. Executive condominiums have their own occupation rules. ([How to Sell a Condo in Singapore: Steps & Costs](https://joetay.com/insights/how-to-sell-condo-singapore.html))
- Can I rent out my whole HDB flat? Only if you are a Singapore Citizen owner who has met the Minimum Occupation Period, and only with HDB’s approval. Singapore Permanent Resident owners may not rent out a whole flat, and HDB says owners of Prime and Plus flats may not do so even after their 10-year MOP. ([Renting Out an HDB Flat or Condo: The Rules](https://joetay.com/insights/renting-out-hdb-condo-singapore.html))
- Has the 15-month wait-out period been removed? Yes. From 28 July 2026, private property owners and former owners can buy a non-subsidised HDB resale flat of any size without waiting 15 months, provided they do not take an HDB housing loan and sell all private residential property within six months of completing the flat purchase. ([15-Month Wait-Out Removed: What Owners Do Now](https://joetay.com/insights/15-month-wait-out-removed-private-owners-hdb.html))
- Is the HDB income ceiling $18,000 in 2026? No. From 24 August 2026 HFE applications, the general family ceiling for subsidised HDB housing and HDB loans is $16,000. The $18,000 ceiling applies to qualifying new EC sites whose land sale tender closes on or after 24 August 2026. ([HDB Income Ceiling 2026: $16k HDB, $18k EC](https://joetay.com/insights/hdb-income-ceiling-2026-ndr-changes.html))
- Do I need an HFE letter for a resale HDB flat? Yes. A buyer must have a valid HFE letter before obtaining an Option to Purchase from a resale-flat seller and when submitting the resale application. ([HDB Loan Eligibility Singapore (2026)](https://joetay.com/insights/hdb-loan-eligibility-singapore.html))
- What is the MSR limit in Singapore? MSR is capped at 30% of gross monthly income for housing loans used to buy an HDB flat or an executive condominium whose minimum occupation period has not expired. ([MSR vs TDSR Singapore: HDB Loan Limits](https://joetay.com/insights/msr-vs-tdsr-singapore.html))
- How much HDB resale grant can a family receive? The CPF Housing Grant is up to $80,000 for an eligible family buying a 2- to 4-room resale flat or $50,000 for a 5-room or larger flat. EHG and PHG may be added if the household meets their separate conditions. ([HDB Resale Grants Singapore (2026): Amounts](https://joetay.com/insights/hdb-resale-grants-singapore.html))
